relevance_note: Case report of two infants with HLH and germline TNFAIP3 variants: 'we report two children with the primary presentation of HLH, with a mutation in TNFAIP3, in favor of HA20'; Table 3 also summarises two previously published TNFAIP3 patients.
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; values were typed into a Python builder script (no automatic table transcription) and every span was checked verbatim against the Markdown by script. Scope: the two first-hand patients (labels 'Patient one' and 'Patient two', the section headings; Table 3 calls them 'Our patient N. 1/2'); the two tested-negative parents of Patient two ('parent of Patient two', 'parent of Patient two 2'; sex not stated individually; no variant rows because both are homozygous wild type); the two previously published patients in Table 3 rows 1-2 (bare 'Number' column, so 'Table 3 #1' = Li et al. [29] patient, also described in the Discussion text, and 'Table 3 #2' = Takagi et al. [9] patient, also described in text; source_reference_in_review copied from the table's Author cell); and the three patients of Zhang et al. [25] described individually in the Discussion ('ref [25] patient', '... 2', '... 3'), included because the paragraph presents them as HA20 examples, but the paper never prints their variants or explicitly calls them HA20/TNFAIP3 carriers, so no variant rows and disease label 'not reported'. Left out: Patient one's healthy, untested older sister and his untested consanguineous parents (neither tested nor affected); the other three Li et al. patients (count only). Age at diagnosis for Patient one is the age when the WES result was delivered (2 years 4 months); the HLH diagnosis was at presentation (4 months). Patient two's last evaluation is given only as '4 years have passed since the first presentation', not an age, so it is 'not reported'. Patient two is de novo because WES/Sanger covered both parents ('his parents are homozygous wild type'); Takagi's 'de novo mutation of TNFAIP3 was detected' gives no parental testing, so inheritance is 'not reported'. Table 3 '-' in 'Other features' for the paper's own patients is undefined and was not used. Group statements naming 'our patients'/'Both of our patients' (no autoantibodies, no Behcet's-like symptoms, MAS criteria) were applied to both patients as 'inferred from group statement'; the Behcet's-like statement was not used to exclude individual checklist items. Pancytopenia/thrombocytopenia (HLH-related) was not counted as 'cytopenia (autoimmune)'. 'Intermittent fever' was counted as recurrent fever; Patient two's single 'prolonged fever' was not. Patient one's cerebral hemorrhage was counted as central nervous system involvement. Contradictions/inconsistencies: (1) Patient two's protein change is described as 'a proline to leucine amino acid change (p. L275P)', while the notation p.L275P denotes leucine to proline; (2) Patient one: text says 'normal ESR, CRP' but Table 1 shows ESR 11 (range 0-10) and CRP 6 (<6), not asterisked; the text was followed; (3) Li et al. variant printed as 'c.259C > T (p.R87X)' in text (transcript NM_006290) and 'c.C259T, p.R87X' in Table 3; the text form was recorded; (4) Takagi patient: text says pancytopenia, Table 3 says thrombocytopenia (both recorded); (5) Patient two: 'the coagulation profile was normal, except for thrombocytopenia' while fibrinogen was 93* (hypofibrinogenemia listed); (6) Patient two: leukocytosis and thrombocytosis are mentioned only as 'resolved' after etanercept, never when they arose; (7) Background says 'we present a case' although two are reported.
